BUSINESS IT SERVICES

IT consultancy and site surveys.

IT consultancy helps a business turn a technology problem into an achievable plan. HeyDock scopes site assessments, infrastructure reviews and project discovery, with a focus on decisions the business needs to make. A site survey records the agreed observations; it does not automatically certify every system.

Discuss requirementsExplore services

SERVICE EXPLAINED

What does this service involve?

A useful assessment begins with a question. You may be planning an office move, replacing equipment or deciding whether a software project is viable. Defining the decision first keeps the survey focused on relevant evidence rather than collecting an inventory that nobody uses.

The engagement starts by identifying the business outcome, existing responsibilities and the changes you authorise. HeyDock then confirms suitable delivery capacity, the working window and the evidence needed to complete the task. Related licences, hardware, subscriptions and specialist services are included only where the proposal says so.

PRACTICAL SCOPE

What can be included?

The final statement of work identifies the tasks that apply to your environment.

Discovery and current-state review

Gather business goals, affected users, existing systems and constraints. Identify what information is missing and which stakeholders can validate the findings.

Site and infrastructure observations

Record relevant equipment, connectivity, space and access requirements. Agree survey depth, site permissions and any specialist testing before attendance.

Options and implementation planning

Present practical options, dependencies and assumptions. Separate recommendations from confirmed scope, and identify what needs further validation before a delivery commitment.

EXAMPLE REQUIREMENT

How a project might work.

Before an office relocation, a survey can assess desk capacity, network points, meeting rooms and connectivity dependencies. The findings become an implementation brief with owners and an agreed sequence.

PLANNING AND COST

What affects the scope and price?

Cost depends on the number of users, devices or sites; technical complexity; access requirements; delivery hours; travel; and the work needed before and after implementation. Provide relevant system versions and existing supplier responsibilities so the quotation can distinguish labour from licences, equipment and recurring charges.

For a well-defined task, a visit or project quotation may be appropriate. Where important dependencies are unknown, a paid assessment can produce a better implementation scope. Any response, attendance or recovery target must be explicitly agreed; requesting a service does not create an immediate support commitment.

COMMON QUESTIONS

IT consultancy and site surveys FAQs

What do we receive after an assessment?+

The scope can include findings, an inventory, identified gaps and recommended next steps. Required report formats should be agreed upfront.

Can you deliver the resulting project?+

Implementation can be proposed separately once the requirements, capacity and costs are confirmed.

What information should we include in an enquiry?+

Describe the objective, location, affected systems, preferred timing and existing support arrangements. Do not send passwords or sensitive business records in the enquiry form.
